subject: Request: evidence for data purge schedules (logs, backups, prompts) – DPIA/SCCs

Subject: DPIA evidence request — retention & deletion timelines for logs/backups/prompts

Vivek,

As part of our DPIA and SCCs review for the upcoming procurement milestone, our privacy & security team needs concrete evidence of retention and deletion practices for the data categories below for Redwood Inference:

- Operational logs (access, request/response metadata) — retention period and deletion process
- Backups and snapshot rotation — retention windows and secure deletion/overwriting procedures
- Customer prompts & model inputs — whether stored, how long, and how they are deleted on request
- KV/prefix caches and any persistent debugging traces

Can you provide: 
1) A brief written summary of current default retention windows and deletion workflows for each category above
2) Any existing artifact we can attach to our DPIA — SOC 2 mapping extract, internal playbook, or an attestation letter
3) If deletion on customer request (data subject or DPA) requires a manual operation or an automated tenant-level purge, and expected SLA for completion

We need these artifacts by EOD Tue 23 June to keep our procurement timeline. If you prefer, we can accept a short technical note today and follow up with a formal PDF.

Thanks,
Diane

Vivek / Diane / Ethan — forwarding a short technical summary and planned artifacts. High-level answers below (we'll attach formal artifacts as a zip and a one-page summary):

Operational summary (defaults and procedures)
- Operational logs (request/response metadata): default retention = 90 days. Access logs and request metadata are stored in our centralized ELK cluster and rotated daily. Deletion: roll-off is automated by retention policy; for customer-scoped logs we support tenant-scoped purge which will remove entries within 7 business days after a validated DPA request. We provide export evidence (query + checksum) when requested.

- Backups / snapshots: default snapshot rotation = 30 days (daily incremental + weekly full snapshots). Backups are stored encrypted at rest; deletion on rotation performs secure deletion metadata and subsequent block reclamation (secure overwrite depending on underlying cloud provider). For Private deployments we provide customer-specific backup retention configs; for hosted we can apply an exception under contract.

- Prompt / model input retention: by default, Redwood does NOT persist prompt data to long-term storage. Prompts may be present transiently in the serving runtime (in-memory and KV cache) and in ephemeral request logs used for debugging. Transient caches have a default TTL of 3 hours; ephemeral debugging logs (if enabled) follow the operational log retention above. If a customer requires that prompts are not retained at all, we offer a prompt-handling configuration to disable ephemeral logging for that tenant. Deletion on request: full tenant purge for prompt traces is completed within 5 business days once authenticated and scoped.

- KV / prefix caches and tracing: KV caches are in-memory by default and persisted only when configured; if persisted they follow the backup/snapshot policies and can be purged per-tenant via the purge API (SLA 5 business days).

Evidence we will provide: 
1) redwood_data_retention_summary_v1.pdf — single-page retention matrix with timelines (attached)
2) SOC2_mapping_snapshot.zip — extract of relevant CCs that map to retention & deletion controls
3) detailed_purge_playbook.txt — operational runbook for tenant purge requests (includes acceptance criteria and verification steps)

Notes on attestation & formal letters:
- We can provide the documents above as attachments today. For an official signed attestation, that'll need approval from our Compliance Director; we can usually turn that around in ~7 business days.

Please confirm whether MedTech needs the signed attestation or the artifacts are sufficient for the DPIA. If you'd like, we can also schedule a 30-minute technical call to walk through the artifacts.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
